stories.title: Challenges to treatment preparedness among lung cancer patients from a healthcare provider perspective: a mixed-method study
stories.description: We aim to (1) explore the main barriers to treatment faced by lung cancer patients, from a provider’s perspective, and (2) the existing support systems in addition to recommended mitigation strategies to enhance the preparedness process. Our study invol ves 50 surveys and 10 interview responses, in a mixed-method design. We conducted descriptive statistics and thematic analysis through a hybrid inductive-deductive approach. We based our analysis on the Optimal Care Pathways framework and Andersen’s Behavioral Model. The doctors identified challenges to patient readiness for treatment, such as a lack of knowledge about treatment options, emotional load, logistical barriers (e.g., transportation), and financial pressure. The providers mentioned some initiatives adopted to try to address these challenges, namely in-person instruction, printed materials, and transportation services provided by social workers. However, they emphasized the potential role of accessible digital tools to complement existing educational and support processes. Our results highlight the need to create educational protocols that are standardized yet phase-specific to address the challenges of each treatment phase. These suggestions may improve overall therapy results, decrease delays, and increase patient adherence.

stories.title: Experimental design and analysis of sulfide-induced invasive growth in wine yeast
stories.description: Yeast’s ability to invade surfaces has important implications for infections and food contamination. Invasive growth in yeast is influenced by genetic and environmental factors. In this exploratory study, we used a systematic experimental design to identify conditions under which sulfide-induced invasive growth can be reliably observed and quantified and investigated the effects of sulfide, gene deletions, and environmental conditions on the invasive behaviour of the wine yeast strain AWRI 796. Sulfide enhanced invasion in the (parent) AWRI 796 strain under nitrogen-limiting conditions, although its effect was obscured by experimental variability and pre-culture conditions. Genetic factors had a major effect on the overall invasive phenotype, with deletion of key genes suppressing invasion. Most gene-deletion mutants did not significantly affect how the colony responded to sulfide. In addition to sulfide and genotype, environmental conditions also influenced invasive behaviour. The pre-2 × SLAD pre-culture condition was best for detecting sulfide-induced growth, and later plate washing time and decreased nutrient levels enhanced invasiveness. Our findings suggest that sulfide promotes invasive growth through regulatory mechanisms that are largely independent of the sulfur metabolism and invasive growth genes examined here, providing new insight into the regulation of filamentous growth in wine yeast and a framework for future mechanistic studies.
